questions.q:
In the evolution of the multilateral trading system, consider the following statements:
1. GATT began with 23 founding nations.
2. UNCTAD was founded before the Uruguay Round began.
3. The Marrakesh Agreement came out of the Doha Development Agenda.
4. India joined the WTO only after the Doha Round was launched.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: GATT dates to 1948 and UNCTAD to 1964, well before the Uruguay Round of 1986-94. Statement 3 is wrong because the Marrakesh Agreement of 1994 came from the Uruguay Round, whereas Doha opened in 2001 and remains inconclusive. Statement 4 is wrong because India was a founding member of the WTO in 1995.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The WTO's Appellate Body has been non-functional since 2019.
Statement-II: The WTO's consensus rule allows any single member to block a decision on appointing its judges.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
questions.e: Both are correct and connected. The United States has blocked new appointments, and under consensus one member's objection is enough to stop them. That is why reform proposals include qualified majority voting for appointing members, so that no single State can paralyse dispute settlement. The result is that India's wins at the WTO cannot be enforced in practice against the US or EU.

questions.q:
India's stated negotiating positions at the WTO include which of the following?
1. Restoration of the Appellate Body
2. Preserving public food stockholding flexibilities
3. Preserving TRIPS flexibilities for affordable generics
4. Withdrawal of special and differential treatment from large emerging economies
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: India seeks revival of the Appellate Body, food-stock flexibility under the Agreement on Agriculture, and TRIPS room for affordable generics. Statement 4 is the demand of advanced economies, who argue that China and India should not enjoy such exemptions; India sees its erosion as a threat to farm support such as minimum support prices and food stocks.

questions.q: Which one of the following best describes 'friend-shoring'?
o: Moving supply chains to geographically closest countries irrespective of political ties
Relocating value chains to allied countries on strategic grounds
Bringing production back to the home country through subsidies
Sharing production among members of a customs union to meet rules of origin
questions.e: Friend-shoring moves value chains to allies, reflecting a shift from lowest cost to national security and strategic autonomy. Moving to nearby countries is near-shoring, a close but different idea. Bringing production home is reshoring. The customs-union description concerns preferential rules, not this trend. The China+1 strategy, which could benefit Indian electronics, textiles and chemicals, belongs to the same broad shift.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 21-22; reshoring is static

questions.q:
As regards pressures on the global trading system, consider the following statements:
1. India is a party to RCEP and draws preferential access in the Asia-Pacific from it.
2. The EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism affects Indian exports such as steel, aluminium and cement.
3. The WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement can reduce customs costs for small exporters.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. India stayed out of RCEP, and doing so carries a risk of trade diversion against it in the Asia-Pacific, so statement 1 fails. The EU mechanism is seen by India as a unilateral green barrier, threatening about 8 billion dollars of exports. The facilitation pact helps MSMEs in particular, and is listed among India's opportunities.

questions.q:
With reference to the Agreements on Reciprocal Trade signed by the United States, as reported in February 2026, consider the following statements:
1. They rest on Article XXIV of GATT.
2. They are notified to the WTO for scrutiny in the same way as free trade agreements.
3. The US-Bangladesh agreement obliges Bangladesh to support US national-security trade action with restrictive measures of its own.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 3 is correct. These agreements do not rest on Article XXIV, the provision governing free trade areas and customs unions, and that is why their legality is questioned. They are not notified to the WTO. They also let the US keep tariffs inconsistent with its WTO obligations while partners cut theirs. The El Salvador text limits duties on electronic transactions.

questions.q:
Under WTO rules on preferential trade, consider the following statements:
1. Free trade areas and customs unions are permitted as exceptions to the Most-Favoured-Nation principle.
2. Such agreements must cover substantially all trade.
3. Customs unions, unlike free trade areas, need a common external trade policy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. Most-Favoured-Nation treatment requires that a preference given to one WTO member be extended to all, so these agreements are carved-out exceptions on conditions. Free trade areas let each member keep its own outside tariffs, while customs unions need a shared external policy. Many newer pacts go WTO-plus by adding labour, environment and investment rules.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 44-46; GATT Article XXIV is static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: India's export basket now has far wider coverage under free trade agreements than in 2019.
Statement-II: India's strategy shifted to comprehensive agreements with advanced economies after opting out of RCEP.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and linked. Coverage of exports is projected to rise from about 22 per cent in 2019 to about 71 per cent in 2026. After staying out of RCEP, India moved from cautious deals with similar economies to comprehensive arrangements with advanced economies such as Australia, the UAE and the UK, and concluded talks with the EU, pairing these with production-linked incentives and infrastructure.

questions.q:
As regards India's trading partners, consider the following pairs:
Trade partner : Position in India's trade, as reported
1. China : India's largest source of imports
2. Netherlands : Among India's top export destinations
3. Malaysia : India's third largest trading partner in ASEAN
4. France : India's largest trading partner in the EU
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. France is India's third largest trading partner in the EU, after the Netherlands and Germany, so pair 4 fails. The top export destinations are listed as the US, UAE, Netherlands and UK. The top import sources are China, Russia, UAE and the US. Trade with France, at about 12.67 billion euro, is described as thin.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 46-48; Vision IAS pp. 23-24, 27

questions.q:
In the context of the Gulf Cooperation Council, consider the following statements:
1. Iraq and Yemen are among its members.
2. Its Supreme Council has an attached Commission for Settlement of Disputes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the six members are the UAE, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar and Kuwait. Its main organs are the Supreme Council, the Ministerial Council and the Secretariat General. India and the Council signed a Framework Agreement on Economic Cooperation in New Delhi in 2004, and have now finalised Terms of Reference for a free trade agreement.

questions.q:
With reference to India-France cooperation, consider the following pairs:
Project : Partners
1. H125 helicopter Final Assembly Line : Tata and Airbus
2. HAMMER smart munitions joint venture : Hindustan Aeronautics Limited and Dassault Aviation
3. TRISHNA satellite : ISRO and CNES
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct. The HAMMER venture is between Bharat Electronics Limited and Safran, within the 2024 Defence Industrial Roadmap's push for co-production, so pair 2 fails. The H125 line, announced during the French President's visit, is India's first private-sector helicopter facility. TRISHNA is an earlier joint satellite project of the two space agencies.

questions.q:
With reference to the amendment of the India-France Double Taxation Avoidance Convention, 1992, consider the following statements:
1. It incorporates provisions of the BEPS Multilateral Instrument.
2. It removes the Most-Favoured-Nation clause.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. The Multilateral Instrument is an OECD tool against base erosion and profit shifting, used to update tax treaties without renegotiating each one separately. Removing the Most-Favoured-Nation clause closes a route by which a partner could claim better terms that India had given another country. Note that this is a tax-treaty clause, separate from WTO non-discrimination.

questions.q:
With reference to the India-France relationship, consider the following statements:
1. The Strategic Partnership dates from 2008.
2. The civil nuclear agreement dates from 1998.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct, as the two dates are interchanged. The Strategic Partnership was established in 1998, the year of India's nuclear tests, and the civil nuclear agreement came in 2008. The Horizon 2047 roadmap followed in 2023. The relationship is often cited as a case of strategic autonomy with a Western power, with the Jaitapur nuclear project in Maharashtra as a long-running element.

questions.q:
In respect of India's military exercises, consider the following pairs:
Exercise : Participants
1. VARUNA : India and France (navies)
2. Harimau Shakti : India and Malaysia
3. LAMITYE : India and Seychelles
4. La Perouse : Bilateral Indian and French armies
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. La Perouse is a multilateral exercise, as is ORION, while the army exercise with France is FRINJEX, so pair 4 fails. Harimau Shakti reached its fifth edition in the context of the Prime Minister's Malaysia visit. LAMITYE is the joint exercise cited alongside maritime cooperation with Seychelles, and VARUNA is the naval exercise with France.

questions.q: In February 2026, India and Israel agreed on an initiative on Critical and Emerging Technologies. Which one of the following correctly identifies who leads it?
o: The two Science and Technology Ministers
questions.e: The two National Security Advisers lead it, covering AI, cybersecurity, semiconductors, quantum, biotechnology and space, with a Memorandum of Understanding on AI and a horizon-scanning mechanism. Leadership at this level shows how technology is treated as a strategic matter. The foreign ministers' dialogue mentioned this month belongs to India-France ties, and the defence and science ministers are plausible but wrong here.

questions.q:
With reference to India-Israel relations, consider the following statements:
1. The two countries cooperate in the I2U2 grouping, whose other members are the UAE and the US.
2. India established full diplomatic relations with Israel in 1950.
3. The India-Israel Innovation Centre for Agriculture was agreed through a Memorandum of Understanding.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 merges two dates: India recognised Israel in 1950, while full diplomatic ties came in 1992. I2U2 groups India, Israel, the UAE and the US, and both countries also cooperate on the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor. The ties were upgraded to a Special Strategic Partnership for Peace, Innovation and Prosperity.

questions.q: The Su-30 Forum, in the news during the Prime Minister's visit in February 2026, relates to technical and maintenance cooperation between the air forces of India and:
questions.e: It is a forum between the air forces of India and Malaysia, both of which operate Su-30 variants. Malaysia and India also created a Strategic Affairs Working Group, and ties rose to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in August 2024. The other three countries are important defence partners of India in their regions, which makes them tempting but incorrect answers.

questions.q:
With reference to Seychelles and India, consider the following statements:
1. Seychelles will become a full member of the Colombo Security Conclave.
2. Seychelles will join the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure.
3. Seychelles will recognise the Indian Pharmacopoeia.
4. India's plan to develop Assumption Island concerns surveillance near sea lanes such as the Mozambique Channel.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. The Conclave addresses shared transnational threats and also includes India, Sri Lanka, Mauritius, the Maldives and Bangladesh. Recognising the book of drug standards helps supply affordable quality medicines. Assumption Island and a coastal radar network reflect India's interest in the western Indian Ocean under Vision MAHASAGAR, with China's influence in the region as background.

questions.q:
Regarding the western Indian Ocean, consider the following statements:
1. Assumption Island is part of Mauritius.
2. Reunion Island, a French territory, is relevant to India's surveillance options under the India-France Indo-Pacific Roadmap.
3. The Mozambique Channel lies between Mozambique and Madagascar.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Assumption Island belongs to Seychelles, which is why India's plan to develop it features in India-Seychelles ties; candidates may confuse it with Mauritius' Agalega. The Channel is a critical sea line of communication. Reunion offers surveillance options as India's outlook widened from the Indian Ocean Region to the Indo-Pacific. These links show how island diplomacy supports maritime domain awareness.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 23-24, 27-28; Madagascar, Agalega and Reunion's status are static

questions.q:
Which of the following groupings have both India and Brazil as members?
1. BASIC
2. IBSA
3. G-4
4. Five Eyes
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: India and Brazil are together in BASIC on climate, IBSA with South Africa, and the G-4 on Security Council reform, as well as BRICS and the G-20. Five Eyes is the intelligence alliance of the US, the UK, Canada, Australia and New Zealand, and includes neither. Trade links run through the India-MERCOSUR Preferential Trade Agreement, with a revised target of USD 30 billion.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 28; Shankar IAS pp. 48-50

questions.q:
Regarding the Global Biofuel Alliance and the International Solar Alliance, consider the following statements:
1. Brazil is a co-founder of the Global Biofuel Alliance.
2. France is co-president of the International Solar Alliance with India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. The Biofuel Alliance was co-founded by India and Brazil among others, drawing on Brazil's long experience with ethanol. India and France jointly lead the Solar Alliance, a partnership seen as linking Western capital with the energy needs of the Global South. Brazil ratified the Solar Alliance agreement in 2022, so it too is a participant.

questions.q:
With reference to India-Canada relations, which of the following statements are correct?
1. Canada is part of both the G7 and Five Eyes.
2. The Joint Working Group on Counter Terrorism dates from February 2018.
3. Pharmaceuticals and iron and steel are India's main imports from Canada.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. The working group dates from 1997; February 2018 is the framework on Countering Terrorism and Violent Extremism, which built on it. Statement 3 reverses the trade: pharmaceuticals and iron and steel are India's exports to Canada, while Canada supplies pulses, potash and minerals. Canada also joined Australia and India in a trilateral technology partnership.

questions.q:
Which of the following statements about India-Canada ties are correct?
1. Canada is among India's five largest sources of FDI, as per DPIIT data.
2. Indians form the largest group of international students in Canada.
3. Pro-Khalistan groups are reported to be concentrated in Montreal and Quebec City.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct; students numbered over 3.9 lakh at the end of 2024. Canada ranks 17th among investors, with about 0.56 per cent of total FDI, so statement 1 fails. The concentration reported is in Brampton in Ontario and in Vancouver and Surrey in British Columbia, so statement 3 fails. Radicals are estimated to be a small minority of the diaspora.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Kimberley Process:
Statement-I: India holds strategic leverage in the global diamond trade though it is not a significant producer of rough diamonds.
Statement-II: India imports about 40 per cent of the world's rough diamonds and is the leading cutting and polishing hub.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: Both are correct and connected. India's leverage comes from processing, not mining: Surat and Mumbai cut and polish the stones that are then re-exported to markets such as Hong Kong, the UAE and the US. Over 85 per cent of rough production comes from Angola, Botswana, Canada, Congo, Namibia and Russia. India's nodal agency is the Gem and Jewellery Export Promotion Council.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a major criticism of the Kimberley Process that India's reform agenda as Chair in 2026 seeks to address?
o: Its definition of conflict diamonds is confined to rebel financing against governments
It has no certificate requirement for rough diamond consignments
It covers only polished diamonds and leaves rough stones out
It has no civil society participation in its structure
questions.e: The narrow definition ignores state-linked abuses, human rights and environmental harm, and India proposes a technical working group on violence and rights risks. The other three are false: every consignment does need a certificate, the scheme concerns rough diamonds and covers about 99.8 per cent of output, and civil society is one of its three pillars. Consensus also limits reform.

questions.q:
In the Kimberley Process Certification Scheme, consider the following statements:
1. Participants may trade certified rough diamonds freely with non-participants.
2. Each EU member state counts as a separate participant.
3. The Central African Republic, banned from exports in 2013, has not been readmitted.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. Trade is allowed only between compliant members, with a certificate on every consignment. The EU and its member states count as one participant, which is why 60 participants represent 80 countries. The Central African Republic rejoined in 2024; its ban without support is said to have raised smuggling and violence, the lesson India cites in pressing for technical hubs in Africa.

questions.q:
With reference to the Strait of Hormuz, consider the following statements:
1. It lies in the territorial waters of Iran and Oman.
2. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline carries crude to the Red Sea, avoiding the strait.
3. The UAE's pipeline to Fujairah reaches a port inside the Persian Gulf.
4. Iran has fully blockaded the strait on several past occasions.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Fujairah lies outside the Gulf, which is the whole point of that pipeline, so statement 3 fails. Iran has often threatened closure but has not fully blockaded the strait, not even during the 12-day war with Israel, since closure would also hurt its own exports. The bypass pipelines have limited capacity.

questions.q: Which one of the following countries does not rely on the Strait of Hormuz for most of its crude exports, as per the US Energy Information Administration's account of the strait?
questions.e: Nigeria is an OPEC member too, but it exports from the Gulf of Guinea on the Atlantic side. Saudi Arabia, Iran, the UAE, Kuwait and Iraq send most of their crude through the strait, mainly to Asia, and Qatar sends most of its LNG this way. China, India, Japan and South Korea take about two-thirds of the flows.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 40-42; Nigeria's coast is static

questions.q: The Asia Power Index, from which the Power Gap score cited in the Economic Survey 2025-26 is derived, is produced by which one of the following?
o: Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, Sweden
International Institute for Strategic Studies, UK
questions.e: Australia's Lowy Institute produces it annually, and the Power Gap is a secondary analysis comparing resources with influence. India's score of minus 4.0 in the 2025 edition suggests it is operating below its full strategic potential. The other three bodies are prominent security or policy institutions, and SIPRI in particular is known for its arms-transfer data.

questions.q:
With regard to naval cooperation, consider the following statements:
1. The Indian Ocean Naval Symposium was initiated by the Indian Navy in 2008.
2. Combined Maritime Forces is a UN-mandated military alliance with binding contributions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct, and India took up the chairmanship of this voluntary forum of 25 nations. Statement 2 is wrong: Combined Maritime Forces describes itself as a coalition of the willing with voluntary, flexible contributions, and it counters illicit non-state actors. India's recent first-ever command was of its training task force, one of several task forces under the arrangement.

questions.q:
With reference to conflict geography, consider the following statements:
1. Donetsk and Luhansk are in western Ukraine, along the Polish border.
2. The Strait of Kerch links the Sea of Azov with the Caspian Sea.
3. The Erez crossing connects Gaza with Egypt.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. The two regions form the Donbas in eastern Ukraine, with Russia to the east. The Strait of Kerch links the Sea of Azov with the Black Sea, not the Caspian. Erez leads from northern Gaza into Israel; it is Rafah in the south that borders Egypt's Sinai Peninsula. Careless map reading produces these confusions.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 30-31; Erez leading to Israel is static

questions.q:
With reference to critical-minerals initiatives launched by the United States, consider the following statements:
1. FORGE succeeds the Minerals Security Partnership.
2. India stayed away from the ministerial meeting at which FORGE was launched.
3. Project Vault is a stockpile run directly by the US Department of Defense without private participation.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. FORGE, the Forum on Resource, Geostrategic Engagement, came out of the inaugural Critical Minerals Ministerial in Washington, where delegations from over fifty countries included India. Project Vault establishes the US Strategic Critical Minerals Reserve as an independently governed public-private partnership that buys and stores critical minerals and rare earths, so statement 3 also fails.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Intercontinental ballistic missiles
2. Submarine-launched ballistic missiles
3. Heavy bombers
4. Tactical nuclear weapons
How many of the above were limited by the New START Treaty?
questions.e: The first three categories were limited, along with a cap of 1,550 deployed strategic warheads on each side. Tactical or non-strategic weapons lay outside it, a well-known gap in US-Russia arms control. Signed in 2010 and in force from 2011, it was the last legally binding bilateral nuclear arms-control treaty between the two largest arsenals.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 30; tactical weapons exclusion is static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The As Low As Reasonably Achievable approach calls for minimising radiation dose even below statutory limits.
Statement-II: The Linear No-Threshold model assumes that any dose of radiation carries some cancer risk.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
questions.e: Both are correct, and the second underpins the first. If no dose is assumed entirely safe, it makes sense to keep exposure as low as reasonably achievable, balancing social and economic factors. The US Department of Energy's move away from this approach towards a risk-informed one raises concern of higher worker exposure, since nothing then requires doses below statutory limits.

questions.q: Arctic Sentry, launched in February 2026, is a mission of which one of the following, led through which command?
o: NATO, through Joint Force Command Norfolk
Arctic Council, through its Sustainable Development Working Group
European Union, through its Military Staff
United States Northern Command, under a bilateral arrangement with Canada
questions.e: It is a NATO mission led by Joint Force Command Norfolk, which NATO treats as its bridge between North America and Europe. Its stated aim is protecting members and territory amid rising Russian military activity and growing Chinese interest in the Arctic. The Arctic Council does not handle military matters, and neither US Northern Command nor the EU leads this mission.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 30; Arctic Council mandate is static

questions.q:
With reference to places in the news in February 2026, consider the following pairs:
Place : Geographical description
1. Rafah Crossing : Connects Gaza with Egypt's Sinai Peninsula
2. Donetsk : Borders the Sea of Azov to its south
3. Diego Garcia : Largest island in the Chagos Archipelago
4. El-Fasher : Located in the Darfur region of Sudan
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All four are correct. Rafah is Gaza's southernmost exit; Erez and Kerem Shalom are the other crossings. Donetsk and Luhansk form the Donbas, and the Sea of Azov links to the Black Sea via the Strait of Kerch. Diego Garcia hosts a UK-US base. El-Fasher, whose siege by a paramilitary group brought reports of genocide, is in Darfur, as is the Zamzam camp.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 30-31; El-Fasher in Darfur is static

questions.q:
Regarding the Chagos Archipelago, consider the following statements:
1. Diego Garcia, its largest island, hosts a joint UK-US military base.
2. In February 2026 the United States urged the United Kingdom not to hand it to Mauritius.
3. The archipelago lies south-west of Mauritius.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The archipelago lies north-east of Mauritius in the Indian Ocean, so statement 3 fails. The US position cut across the 2025 arrangement under which the UK would return the islands while keeping the base. For India, the issue combines decolonisation with Indian Ocean security, which is why it matters beyond the two parties involved.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Asian importers would bear the most direct supply risk from a disruption in the Strait of Hormuz.
Statement-II: China, India, Japan and South Korea together account for about two-thirds of the oil flows through the strait.
Statement-III: Iran's coastline runs along the entire northern side of the strait.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both of them explain Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct, but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
questions.e: All three are correct, but only Statement-II explains Statement-I. About 82 per cent of crude and condensate through the strait went to Asia in 2022, so a shock hits Asian buyers first. Statement-III is true and explains Iran's leverage over shipping, not who bears the risk. For India, over 40 per cent of oil supplies come from Gulf States using this route.

questions.q: The Iran-Pakistan-India 'Peace Pipeline', mentioned in a suggested reframing of India's foreign policy, was conceived to transport which one of the following?
questions.e: It was proposed as a natural gas pipeline from Iran through Pakistan to India, and the suggestion here is that its revival would earn Pakistan transit fees and help treat ties as a foreign-policy matter rather than only a security one. It was never a crude or product line, and hydrogen transport is a much later idea, so those distractors are plausible only superficially.

questions.q:
On India-US economic ties as reported in February 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The United States was described as India's third largest investor.
2. India runs a trade deficit with the United States.
3. Bilateral trade in FY25 exceeded that of FY24.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. India runs a trade surplus with the United States, so statement 2 is wrong; this surplus is part of why reciprocal tariffs became an issue. Cumulative FDI from 2000 to 2025 was USD 70.65 billion. Bilateral trade reached a record USD 132.2 billion in FY25, up from USD 119.71 billion.
